entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5842"/><title type="x-s2">PSALM 35</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Ps.35.1-Ps.35.28">Psa 35:1-28</reference>. The Psalmist invokes God's aid, contrasting the hypocrisy, cunning, and malice of his enemies with his integrity and generosity. The imprecations of the first part including a brief notice of their conduct, the fuller exposition of their hypocrisy and malice in the second, and the earnest prayer for deliverance from their scornful triumph in the last, are each closed (<reference osisRef="Ps.35.9">Psa 35:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.10.18">10, 18</reference>, 27, 28) with promises of praise for the desired relief, in which his friends will unite. The historical occasion is probably <reference osisRef="1Sam.24.1-1Sam.24.22">1Sa 24:1-22</reference>.</title> <div sID="gen8890" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5842"/>1-3. God is invoked in the character of a warrior (<reference osisRef="Exod.15.3">Ex 15:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.32.41">De 32:41</reference>). <div eID="gen8890" type="x-p"/>

Halting, or, "lameness," as in Psa 38:17 for any distress. abjects-- either as cripples (compare 2Sa 4:4 ), contemptible; or, degraded persons, such as had been beaten (compare Job 30:1-8 ).
